GOV.reason: Disclosed connected deployment and minority dilution warrant restraint; detailed entity accounts and clean dated secretarial review are counterevidence to any claim of proven abuse. Bank differences and benefits/accounting presentation prevent a high score.

MOAT.reason: Regional distribution, service and own-brand assembly support customer access; value-added profit grew. No independently verified pricing premium, market share or customer retention establishes a structural moat, and product competition/input sourcing remain substantial.

REV.reason: Use FY2023–26 parent CAGR28.28% as the less pandemic-affected constant-parent basis: starting 8, no trajectory bonus. Five-year35.06% is shown, not cherry-picked to score 9. Rising group material value added supports economic expansion; price/volume and industry-relative growth remain unseparated. Medium confidence ceiling 8 applies.

DUR.reason: TV, fan, cooler and IFPD channels create several accessible avenues with disclosed assembly capacity and distributors. Backward integration is not new TV assembly capacity, and funding, customer conversion and commissioned utilization are not yet demonstrated.

CAP.reason: Three/five-year NOPAT-to-capital-increase proxies near 10.63% and one-year 8.86% do not demonstrate returns above an analyst 12–16% nominal INR cost-of-capital range. Current average-capital ROIC is about15.05%, while recent CWIP is immature; favorable utilization could improve outcomes, so this is mixed evidence rather than proven permanent destruction.

CASH.reason: Adjusted parent CFO is negative in each FY2024–26 and three-year conversion is −1.2442; group two-year conversion −0.7998 and receivables expanded sharply. Inventory release and management collection assertions are counterpoints, but neither reverses the persistent cash pattern. GQS cash cap 5 applies.

BAL.reason: March debt₹25.7632 crore is modest against reported EBITDA₹19.0322 crore and ordinary no-expansion stress survives. Cash₹0.2573 crore is very small, demand debt is material and aged-collection stress exposes an unfunded gap unless headroom exists. No current default is established.

EXEC.reason: Historical sales and IFPD/brand launch milestones establish execution, not just plans. January 2027 backward integration, below 90-day collections and utilization targets remain unverified. Final migration is not inferred from in-principle approval.

EARN.reason: FY26 group operating EBIT₹18.0855 crore and profit₹12.2047 crore rise with sales, rather than large current other income. Issue dilution, higher marketing and lower material-value-added margin temper per-share quality; FY25 parent printed EPS is not bonus-comparable without correction.

R.reason: A complete funded diagnostic exists, but it depends on unverified project deployment, facilities, warrant exercise and rescue equity. Central−3.05% is not a defensible endorsed base return; do not assign the mechanicalR 1 or publish an IAS.

D.reason: Ordinary bear conditional terminal price₹16.55 is about 91.6% below₹197.10, and severe equity is zero despite assumed recapitalization. Stable legacy operations can survive without expansion; that countercase prevents equating expansion financing failure with inevitable insolvency.

P.reason: Current issued-share earnings cost 35.23× and EV/EBITDA23.93×. At the central reinvestment/margin/exit framework, scanning0–80% annual growth never meets15% because funding and dilution absorb growth. A better bull outcome requires margins, working capital and execution to improve together; no precise probability is assigned.

L.reason: 60-session 5%-participation estimate 1.19 days starts at 9. Reduce two points for the ₹197,100 lot and official concentration/irregular-trading warnings, with unobserved live depth. Eligible SM trading and 60 observed sessions oppose an untradeability finding.

IAS.note: Mathematical missing-factor bounds, not confidence intervals.

score_note: BQS 4.84; GQS raw 6.10, capped at 5.00 for persistent CASH 2; IAS NS because R is unsupported. Displayed using half-up one decimal. Historical quality rankings are eligible; investment ranking is not.

confidence.overall: low for an investment conclusion; medium for historical BQS/GQS
confidence.forecast_uncertainty: High and distinct from historical evidence confidence.

gates.reason: No substantiated diversion or severe minority harm established. Connected claims, financing terms and presentation weaknesses warrant monitoring; disclosed RPTs alone are not misconduct.

The material cash/debt and fixed-asset totals reconcile to signed entity accounts. Mixed GAAP/Ind AS wording, small note inconsistencies, unquantified benefits and issue-cost detail remain; these bounded historical caveats do not require every quality factor to be NS. They do limit normalization and the forecast.

Expansion cannot be treated as funded from unreceived warrants or assumed facilities. No-expansion ordinary stress survives; delaying the ₹7.0163 crore aged-parent receipt amount creates a modeled₹4.11 crore trough. Actual October collections, cancellation obligations and sanctioned headroom are not verified, so neither a clear stress pass nor an evidenced unfinanceable shortfall is established.

Eligible SM series and dated trades verified.₹5 lakh reference estimate is 1.19 days at 5% participation, but1,000-share lots, unknown depth and next-session official cautions constrain implementation. In-principle migration is not actual main-board admission.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Arham is a regional branded electronics and appliances manufacturer/distributor attempting a larger national platform. Parent sales rose from ₹48.44 crore in FY2023 to ₹102.25 crore in FY2026; group FY2026 sales reached ₹118.57 crore. Its strength is demonstrated distribution-led growth and new-product execution, not a proven structural moat. Its decisive weakness is persistent adjusted operating cash consumption and fresh funding needed for receivables, marketing and integration. At the October 19 close of ₹197.10, the central funded illustration returns −3.05% annually, but it is not a verified base forecast: R and IAS remain NS. This is a funding-sensitive expansion watchlist, not an evidence-backed compounder or an instruction to trade. Verified collections and project financing would matter more than a superficial P/E decline. [S1–S3, A3, A46, M1]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Arham Technologies Limited; NSE SME ARHAM; ISIN INE0L2Y01011. Cutoff October 20, 2026; October 19 close ₹197.10; actual issued shares 2.1812 crore; market capitalization ₹429.91 crore. October 14 migration approval is in principle, not effective main-board admission. The group includes wholly owned Arham Corporate, established in January 2024, with no reported NCI. Its 18.96% Starshine Ventures holding is a separate investment. Accounts describe Indian GAAP/Section 133 but also reference Ind AS 110; consistent Ind AS compliance is not assumed. The horizon is five years, the nominal pre-tax equity hurdle 15%, and ₹5 lakh only a liquidity reference. G1/G2/G4 are conditional; G3 is unresolved funding, not evidenced default. Historical cash reconstruction has High confidence; growth, governance and capital returns Medium; current deployment and valuation Low. Overall investment confidence is Low, while bounded historical quality remains scoreable. [S1, S4, arham_sub26, M1]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 2, BAL 4, EXEC 6 and EARN 6; IAS R NS, D 2, P 2 and L 7. BQS = 1.00 + 0.80 + 0.96 + 0.60 + 0.48 + 0.20 + 0.32 + 0.48 = 4.84, displayed 4.8. GQS = 3.20 + 1.20 + 0.90 + 0.60 + 0.20 = 6.10, capped at 5.00 for persistent CASH 2. Both quality composites have 100% factor coverage. IAS has 65% coverage, known contribution 2.51 and missing-R mathematical bounds 2.86–6.01, not a confidence interval or rankable score. No weights are redistributed. Moving GOV or MOAT by one point changes BQS by 0.20; moving REV by one changes BQS by 0.12 and raw GQS by 0.40, although the current GQS cap remains binding. Factor evidence and contrary findings are linked in the audit. These are judgment conventions, not validated return predictors. [S1–S3, S5]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: Arham sells Smart LED TVs under STARSHINE and economy ARATTON, manufactures or assembles fans and coolers, and distributes other appliances through dealers, distributors and OEM relationships. Purchased components, assembly, branding, service and channel credit drive economics; recognized sales are not cash receipts. Management described FY2026 revenue mix as 65% TVs, 20% fans, 14% coolers and 1% other appliances. That is an attributed mix, not an audited segment table. Management also described roughly 200 active dealers per quarter and 70% of sales from older dealers, not independently verified retention cohorts. Arham Corporate broadens group manufacturing/trading; parent and consolidated revenue must not be mixed into an organic CAGR. Product-level margins, sell-through and quantified customer/supplier concentration remain ND. [S1, A46, A3]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The plausible advantage is regional distribution, service responsiveness and local assembly/logistics. Mechanism: reliable availability through established channels. Evidence: rising sales and management-disclosed dealer expansion. Durability: depends on product quality, service and collection discipline. Failure mode: national brands or assemblers match price, finance and warranty support. Celebrity advertising and an AI-whiteboard feature do not independently establish pricing power or protected IP. Group material-value-added proxy rose from ₹17.40 crore to ₹24.17 crore, but its margin fell from 24.89% to 20.38%, consistent with expansion partly purchased through pricing/mix. Dixon and Amber are contextual manufacturing contrasts mentioned in the issuer call, not same-risk branded peers. The prospectus said no strict listed comparison existed. No unverified peer multiple or independently measured market-share advantage is assumed. [S1, A46, S5]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Standalone FY2020–26 revenue, ₹crore: 13.7837, 22.7549, 36.4679, 48.4432, 54.6898, 65.1575 and 102.2496. Annual additions in FY2021–26 were 8.9712, 13.7130, 11.9753, 6.2466, 10.4677 and 37.0921. Five-year CAGR was 35.06%, but its pandemic-era start and limited volume decomposition counsel against a 9. The less affected constant-parent FY2023–26 CAGR of 28.28% starts REV at 8, with no single-quarter bonus. Group FY2026 revenue grew 69.64%, from ₹69.8935 crore to ₹118.5661 crore; material value added grew 38.90%. This is not called identical to parent organic growth. The Q1FY2027 operational update reported ₹40.40 crore versus ₹18.20 crore; October 1 expected H1 above ₹80 crore versus ₹45.62 crore, not final results. No audited TTM or quarterly CFO is fabricated. Ten-year growth and a verified price/volume split are ND. [S1–S3, S5, A10, A3]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Management cited annual TV assembly capacity of 300,000 units, utilization moving toward 50%, and a 75% FY2028 target. Backward integration adds plastics, metal fabrication and components, not automatically more TV assembly. IFPD production was announced July 24; the separate approximately ₹40 crore unit targeted January 2027 and remained described as on track in October. The 75%/50% utilization ratio offers 1.5× theoretical volume headroom, not a sales forecast. The central diagnostic assumes FY2027 revenue ₹180 crore, below the ₹200 crore management target, then growth of 25/20/15/12/10% to ₹382.54 crore. Beyond FY2028 it funds incremental capacity at 4× sales/capital. This terminal scale exceeds 3.2× FY2026 sales and requires more than utilization alone. It also needs WC falling from 59.3% to 54% of sales, ₹31.31 crore future project cash after the ₹8.69 crore advance, marketing and further capital. GQS is capped at 5 despite strong top-line growth because cash conversion remains persistently weak. [A46, A13, A3, S1]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The Jain family leads the company. March 2026 promoter shares of 12.25 million represent 56.16% of 21.812 million issued shares, versus about 72.40% on the prior base. Annual balance-sheet capital and the security master agree; the secretarial narrative contains a different allotment count, so the actual balance-sheet/share-register basis is used. The April 6 declaration reports no FY2026 encumbrance; it is not an October guarantee. Parent-to-subsidiary funding of ₹10.45 crore loans and ₹9.60 crore equity is eliminated in consolidated economics. Starshine investment ₹4.4998 crore and advance ₹4.9002 crore are separate connected exposures with uncertain realization. CARO says ₹10.50 crore for the subsidiary loan versus ₹10.45 crore in detailed schedules. Bank-stock differences are attributed to valuation methods and inventory complexity, without a quantified bridge; this is not proof of diversion. The August 12 secretarial report identifies no cases or SEBI/exchange action within its scope. June 27 concerned a cost auditor, not statutory-auditor resignation. Audited director salaries total ₹0.3825 crore, versus about ₹0.3380 crore in the remuneration annexure. July 22 AGM approved total annual salary ceilings up to ₹1.84 crore; ceilings are not actual payments. [S1, arham_sub26, A11, A16, A27, A32]

Promises versus delivery: FY2027 sales above ₹200 crore remain a target, with Q1 reported ₹40.40 crore and H1 expected above ₹80 crore; below-90-day debtors lack a verified receipt schedule; IFPD production was announced July 24; the brand campaign launched October 15; January 2027 integration is prospective; migration has only in-principle approval. [A46, A10, A3, A13, A1, S4]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY2026 group revenue/EBITDA/EBIT/PAT were ₹118.5661/19.0322/18.0855/12.2047 crore; operating earnings exclude ₹0.0275 crore other income. Reported CFO of −₹39.7549 crore needs a category bridge: remove ₹10.45 crore intragroup advance, ₹8.2877 crore current-debt repayment, ₹8.69 crore building advance and ₹4.9002 crore connected long advance to obtain analytical after-interest CFO of −₹7.4270 crore. Matching financing/investing adjustments reconcile the actual ₹0.1958 crore cash increase; no missing cash is inferred. Adjusted parent CFO in FY2024–26 was −₹5.2607/8.1611/9.2210 crore, giving cumulative CFO/PAT of −1.2442; group FY2025–26 conversion is −0.7998. FY2026 cash after operating fixed-asset outflow ₹27.8650 crore and building advance ₹8.69 crore is approximately −₹43.98 crore, before separate connected deployment. Capex does not excuse negative CFO.

Group receivables of ₹57.5887 crore imply 112.55 average days or 177.28 closing days using total revenue: distinct denominators, not contradictory facts. Parent balances of ₹7.0163 crore exceed six months, not automatically bad debt. Opening ONWC of ₹70.3169 crore includes ordinary operating, statutory and expense claims. Gross tax ₹3.3998 crore less entity-matched advance tax ₹3.39 crore leaves ₹0.0098 crore to settle; remaining tax/TDS credits of ₹0.1063 crore receive no base cash value. Debt ₹25.7632 crore, deferred tax ₹0.0202 crore and benefit exposure are retained. Accounts disclose unmeasured gratuity and non-compliance with AS 15; our ₹0.25 crore terminal reserve and ₹1 crore sensitivity are assumptions, not quantified issuer liabilities. Fixed assets of ₹35.4718 crore reconcile to entity schedules within ₹0.0027 crore despite incomplete group-note presentation.

IC of ₹114.4787 crore includes CWIP and advances, versus ₹60.9622 crore a year earlier. At 27% normalized tax, incremental proxies are 8.86% over one year and 10.63% over three/five years, versus an analytical 12–16% cost-of-capital range; average-capital ROIC is 15.05%. The early parent-to-new-subsidiary perimeter is disclosed. Current-issued-share group EPS of ₹5.5954 differs from weighted-average diluted EPS ₹6.87. FY2025 parent printed EPS ₹7.04 uses a pre-bonus denominator; approximately ₹3.52 on the doubled base is the relevant comparison, not a fabricated EPS collapse. [S1–S3, S5, arham_sub25, arham_sub26]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹197.10, current-issued-share P/E is 35.23×, EV/EBITDA 23.93× and book excluding warrants ₹43.45/share. These use March debt/cash, not purported October balances. The model has 67 monthly periods from March 31, 2026 to October 31, 2031; the first seven months are an estimated bridge, not actuals. Bear/central/bull FY2027 revenue is ₹160/180/220 crore; terminal revenue ₹218.10/382.54/582.15 crore; pre-incremental-marketing EBITDA margins 13/17/20%; terminal WC 76/54/44% of sales; exit EV/EBIT 7/11/15×. It deducts marketing, depreciation, 27% cash tax, interest on drawn debt, maintenance, growth investment, principal and all legacy claims. Rescue equity incurs 5% fees at 50% of entry price, an assumed mechanism rather than a committed issue. Warrants add 1,715,795 shares and ₹11.4374894 crore only on assumed April 2027 exercise; 29,000 options at ₹10 are a conservative minimum-price assumption. Connected assets recover 0/50/100% of ₹9.4 crore separately from operating EV. No dividend is double-counted.

Conditional terminal prices ₹16.55/168.69/509.22 imply annual returns of −38.88/−3.05/+20.76%. Gross rescue equity is ₹76.04/52.76/38.19 crore, plus hypothetical pre-entry bridges ₹24.98/17.10/25.25 crore. Without new funding, expansion paths turn cash-negative and show no IRR. Scanning 0–80% constant growth after FY2027 fails to reach a 15% return at central margins/reinvestment and 11× exit; the maximum modeled IRR is 2.23%. Conditional entry solutions for 12/15/18% hurdles are ₹72.25/57.67/45.22, assuming rescue pricing moves with entry. They are not investable targets. Treating the project budget as inclusive of prior IFPD CWIP, with depreciation overlap removed, changes central IRR to −0.33%; extra ₹5 crore annual marketing gives −6.64%; impairment of the aged-parent amount gives −3.52%. R/IAS remain NS until funding and deployment are evidenced. [S1, A46, A3, A50, A8, M1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest loss path is channel expansion → slower collections → WC funding → project and advertising demands → expensive debt or dilution, while competition restrains margins. The ordinary funded bear loses about 91.6% of entry value. Severe combined stress exhausts common equity despite assumed rescue capital, but combines several adverse conditions and has no assigned probability. The counterargument matters: stopping optional expansion and holding ordinary WC fixed leaves the existing business cash-positive under unchanged economics and under 10% lower revenue with a 13% EBITDA margin. A temporary delay of the disclosed ₹7.0163 crore aged-parent receipt amount creates a ₹4.11 crore trough without assuming permanent loss or duplicating replacement costs. That is a modeled liquidity demand, not actual default. Unknown cancellation rights, later receipts and sanctioned headroom keep G3 unresolved rather than automatically failed. The thesis-break variable is verified cash realization plus funding for obligations that cannot be deferred. [S1, A46, A50]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Speculative/unsupported. Five-year 5×/10× price appreciation requires about 38.0%/58.5% annual growth in shareholder value, not merely revenue; ten-year 10× requires 25.9%. Even the demanding bull reaches only ₹509.22 versus ₹197.10, or 2.58×, after debt and dilution. Central modeled shares rise from 2.1812 crore to 2.8911 crore, so enterprise growth materially outruns per-share growth. A credible larger outcome needs demonstrated incremental returns, better collections, funded capacity and sustained brand economics, rather than assumed multiple expansion. [S1, A46, M1]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold: unresolved funding and return evidence. BQS 4.84 and GQS 5.00 describe mixed-quality, cash-intensive expansion; IAS is NS, so no numerical investment-matrix cell is assigned. This is not an evidence-backed compounder: moat, capital returns, cash and balance-sheet factors fall below the designation thresholds. Historical quality comparisons can use the disclosed scores; investment rankings must not substitute the conditional IRR or treat NS as a proven low score. Action category: research/watchlist pending receipts, commitments and financing evidence. No holdings, portfolio weights, tax basis or executable spread were supplied, so no buy/sell or portfolio-exit instruction follows. Price alone cannot cure an unfunded obligation. [S1, A46, A50, M1]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The source ledger links FY2024–26 annual reports, the 2022 prospectus, signed subsidiary accounts, current operating/capital disclosures and official dated market files, with dates and inspected locators. “Partial” means relevant parts, not every page, were read. Retained source tensions include mixed Indian GAAP/Ind AS wording, the ₹10.50/10.45 crore loan narrative, a ₹0.0027 crore fixed-asset presentation difference, ₹2.18 crore unitemized gross/net issue bridge, one warrant in a count, remuneration presentation and bonus-inconsistent parent EPS. None is labeled missing cash or fraud. The model’s tax, project envelope, WC path, issue pricing, capital-cost range and recoveries are analyst assumptions. No current rating/committed facility schedule or fresh numerical peer set is asserted. Actual receipts, irrevocable payments, sanctioned headroom, conversion and employee-benefit measurement are decisive open questions for IAS. [S1–S5, A3, A46, A50, arham_sub26, M1]
